notice.name: Blue Origin Mission Page
notice.raw:
NG-2 Update: We are scheduled to launch Thursday, November 13, with a launch window from 2:57 PM – 4:25 PM EST / 19:57 – 21:25 UTC. The live webcast starts at T-20 minutes.
New Glenn's second mission will launch from Launch Complex 36 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station and will send NASA’s ESCAPADE twin spacecraft to Mars. This launch will support ESCAPADE’s science objectives as the twin spacecraft progress on their journey to the Red Planet. Also onboard is a technology demonstration from Viasat in support of NASA’s Communications Services Project.

notice.name: SpaceX Mission Page
notice.raw:
On Sunday, September 13 at 2:49 p.m. ET, SpaceX launched the SES O3b mPOWER mission to medium Earth orbit from Space Launch Complex 40 (SLC-40) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. 

This was the 29th flight for the first stage booster supporting this mission, which previously supported Ax-2, Euclid, Ax-3, CRS-30, SES ASTRA 1P, NG-21, and 22 Starlink missions. Following stage separation, the first stage landed on the A Shortfall of Gravitas droneship, which was stationed in the Atlantic Ocean.

notice.name: SpaceX Mission Page
notice.raw:
SpaceX is targeting Thursday, October 1 for Falcon Heavy’s launch of the NROL-97 mission from Launch Complex 39A (LC-39A) at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Liftoff is targeted for 11:53 p.m. ET, with a backup opportunity available on Friday, October 2 at 11:48 p.m. ET.

A live webcast of the NROL-97 mission will begin about 10 minutes prior to liftoff, which you can watch here and on X @SpaceX. 

This is the second and fourth flight for the two first stage side boosters supporting this mission, which previously launched the GOES-U, Viasat-3 F3, and Roman Space Telescope missions. Following stage separation, Falcon Heavy’s two side boosters will land on SpaceX’s Landing Zones 1 and 2 (LZ-1 and LZ-2) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.

notice.name: SpaceX Mission Page
notice.raw:
SpaceX’s Falcon 9 is targeting the launch of 27 Starlink satellites to low-Earth orbit from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.

A live webcast of this mission will begin about 10 minutes prior to liftoff, which you can watch here and on X @SpaceX. 

This will be the 20th flight for the first stage booster supporting this mission, which previously launched NROL-126, Transporter-12, SPHEREx, NROL-57, USSF-366, and 14 Starlink missions. Following stage separation, the first stage will land on the Of Course I Still Love You droneship, which will be stationed in the Pacific Ocean.

There is the possibility that residents of Santa Barbara, San Luis Obispo, and Ventura counties may hear one or more sonic booms during the launch, but what residents experience will depend on weather and other conditions.

notice.name: SpaceX Mission Page
notice.raw:
On Saturday, September 19 at 6:47 p.m. PT, Falcon 9 launched 27 Starlink satellites to low-Earth orbit from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.

This was the 17th flight for the first stage booster supporting this mission, which previously launched SDA-T1TL-B, SDA-T1TL-C, Transporter-16, and now 14 Starlink missions. Following stage separation, the first stage landed on the Of Course I Still Love You droneship, which was stationed in the Pacific Ocean.

There was a possibility that residents of Santa Barbara, San Luis Obispo, and Ventura counties may have heard  one or more sonic booms during the launch, but what residents experienced depended on weather and other conditions.

notice.name: SpaceX Mission Page
notice.raw:
On Thursday, September 10 at 8:42 a.m. PT, Falcon 9 launched the USSF-153 mission from Space Launch Complex 4E (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. 

This was the 27th flight for the first stage booster supporting this mission, which previously launched Crew-7, CRS-29, PACE, Transporter-10, EarthCARE, NROL-186, Transporter-13, TRACERS, NROL-48, COSMO-SkyMED Second Generation FM3, and 16 Starlink missions. Following stage separation, the first stage landed on the Of Course I Still Love You droneship, which was stationed in the Pacific Ocean.

There was the possibility that residents of Santa Barbara, San Luis Obispo, and Ventura counties may have heard  one or more sonic booms during the launch, but what residents experienced depended on weather and other conditions.

notice.name: SpaceX Mission Page
notice.raw:
On Wednesday, September 16 at 6:07 p.m. PT, Falcon 9 launched the USSF-259 mission from Space Launch Complex 4E (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. 

This was the 13th flight for the first stage booster supporting this mission which previously launched Sentinel-6B, Twilight, NROL-172, Transporter-17, and eight Starlink missions. Following stage separation, the first stage landed on the Of Course I Still Love You droneship, which was stationed in the Pacific Ocean.

There was the possibility that residents of Santa Barbara, San Luis Obispo, and Ventura counties may have heard  one or more sonic booms during the launch, but what residents experienced depended on weather and other conditions.

notice.name: SpaceX Mission Page
notice.raw:
SpaceX is targeting Saturday, September 26 for a Falcon 9 launch of the USSF-385 mission from Space Launch Complex 4E (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. The three-hour launch window opens at 4:56 a.m. PT. If needed, there is a backup opportunity on Sunday, September 27 at 5:49 a.m. PT. 

A live webcast of the USSF-385 mission will begin about 10 minutes prior to liftoff, which you can watch here and on X @SpaceX. 

This will be the 10th flight for the first stage booster supporting this mission, which previously launched NROL-95 and eight Starlink missions. Following stage separation, the first stage will land on the Of Course I Still Love You droneship, which will be stationed in the Pacific Ocean.

There is the possibility that residents of Santa Barbara, San Luis Obispo, and Ventura counties may hear  one or more sonic booms during the launch, but what residents experience will depend on weather and other conditions.
